summary.oneLiner: Soma Textiles & Industries Limited has transitioned from a closed textile manufacturing operation into a pure-play highway construction company following a change in management and control.
summary.business: Historically engaged in manufacturing cotton yarn, denim fabrics, shirtings, and garments, the Company discontinued its core manufacturing operations due to court-ordered closure of polluting industries in Ahmedabad. It diversified into cotton trading from November 2022 and, after a change in management and control in July 2025, restructured its business to operate solely in the highway construction segment from the quarter ended December 2025.

risks.risk: Execution and operational risks from transition into a new line of business (highway construction)
risks.note: The Company has abruptly shifted from textile trading to infrastructure, exposing it to unfamiliar project execution, cost overruns, and capability gaps.

risks.risk: High working capital requirements and cost overruns in infrastructure projects
risks.note: Infrastructure is capital-intensive with long payment cycles; cost escalations in materials and project delays can strain liquidity and profitability.

risks.risk: Dependence on Holding Company/group entities for project pipeline and business support
risks.note: Revenue and growth are tied to related-party contracts; any change in group strategy or financial health could disrupt operations.

risks.risk: Intense competition in the infrastructure and construction industry
risks.note: The sector has low entry barriers for small projects and established players for large ones, pressuring margins and win rates for a new entrant.

risks.risk: Fluctuation in prices of key construction materials (steel, cement, bitumen, fuel)
risks.note: Input-cost volatility can erode fixed-price contract margins, especially for a company without long-term supplier agreements or scale.

risks.risk: Regulatory and policy risks affecting the infrastructure sector
risks.note: Changes in government spending, approval delays, or environmental clearances can stall projects and impair revenue recognition.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Business continuity and shareholder value preservation through diversification into highway construction after regulatory closure of legacy textile unit.
- Established corporate governance framework compliant with SEBI Listing Regulations, including a vigil mechanism and a board with majority independent directors.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Execution and operational risks from transition into a new line of business (highway construction) — The Company has abruptly shifted from textile trading to infrastructure, exposing it to unfamiliar project execution, cost overruns, and capability gaps.
- High working capital requirements and cost overruns in infrastructure projects — Infrastructure is capital-intensive with long payment cycles; cost escalations in materials and project delays can strain liquidity and profitability.
- Dependence on Holding Company/group entities for project pipeline and business support — Revenue and growth are tied to related-party contracts; any change in group strategy or financial health could disrupt operations.
- Intense competition in the infrastructure and construction industry — The sector has low entry barriers for small projects and established players for large ones, pressuring margins and win rates for a new entrant.
- Fluctuation in prices of key construction materials (steel, cement, bitumen, fuel) — Input-cost volatility can erode fixed-price contract margins, especially for a company without long-term supplier agreements or scale.
- Regulatory and policy risks affecting the infrastructure sector — Changes in government spending, approval delays, or environmental clearances can stall projects and impair revenue recognition.
